name: THE BOX THEATRE · Season One (प्रयोग 01 to 12)
one_line: Every post opens the real blush Naira box: three bells, the drawer slides out, a paper theatre rises inside it, and one real piece takes the stage; twelve shows from Karwa Chauth to the first muhurat, and a grid of twelve little theatres.
big_idea:
THE IDEA IN ONE BREATH. Every Naira piece already arrives in the same blush box: a card sleeve, a drawer, a ribbon pull tab, NAIRA printed on the lid with the flower as the I. Seen from the drawer end it is a proscenium; pulled out, the drawer is a stage. So this season the box becomes a theatre with a cast of one. Every post is a SHOW: three soft bells, the drawer slides out at the website box's own 1.1 s, a layered paper set hinges up inside it (pop-up book, sanjhi cut, laser-cut card, crepe paper), the real piece rises through a trap in the stage floor the way the solitaire rises from its cushion on nairaflore.com, it takes a bow and catches the light, the set folds flat, the drawer slides home, and the programme tells you its name and price. A stranger names it in three seconds: 'the pink jewellery box that turns into a tiny theatre'.

WHY A THEATRE, AND WHY THIS BOX. (1) The box is the one object the buyer, the website and the feed share: it turns above the footer of every page (NairaBox3D), it opens in the bag (BagGiftBox: 'tap to open'), it is in 53 of 56 listings, and every listing promises 'You will receive your piece in a Naira Petite box.' The owner tuned it herself (a 35 s turn, the opening is 'the shopper's'). On Instagram the shopper's tap becomes the shopper's swipe. (2) Packaging is the only topic that ever broke out on this account: 'The Naira Experience' unboxing reel 3,410 likes and 'Unboxing couture, the Naira way' 1,467, against a median of 9.5; packaging-as-product is flagged as an unclaimed lane in Indian demi-fine. (3) The lineage is Indian and adult: the mela bioscope (a painted box you peer into), the Rajasthani kaavad (a box whose doors open to tell a story), Marathi natak (three bells, then the curtain), the toy theatre, the pop-up wedding card. (4) The theatre gives every Indian moment of the season a stage device that is also a joke: the late star (Karwa Chauth), the line he will never say (Bhai Dooj), the understudy (Dhanteras), the lighting rig with one dead bulb (Diwali), the encore (Padwa and Bhaubeej), Tree 3 in the school play (Children's Day), the front row (wedding guests), rehearsals (sangeet), the invitation that came in a box (wedding gifts), the curtain call (the set). Twelve devices, one stage.

THE RULE THAT MAKES IT PREMIUM: ONE REAL THING. Everything on stage is paper except the piece. The set is cut card in the brand's own colours with real paper texture and soft contact shadows; the piece is the photographed, cut-out real listing photo at a believable size inside the box; the box is the real packaging, drawn from the site's own CSS box (same proportions, same card colours, same lid print). Nothing is generated that could be mistaken for jewellery, nobody's face appears, and the motion obeys the box's own house rule: things rise through slots, slide from the wings or hinge up; nothing fades in except light.

THE GRID IS A SHELF OF TWELVE THEATRES. On eleven covers the box sits at the same place and size (600 px wide, its sleeve on a shelf line at y 1046 of the tile), so every row reads as three little theatres on one shelf and the wordmark on the lid is legible at 391x521 (about 135 px wide in the grid; tested in a prototype). The twelve grounds are three colour columns (lac and blush on the left, the lilac aisle in the middle, sage and green on the right) in a value checkerboard that continues LAC / flower / BONE upward; light tiles are MATINEES posted at 12:00, dark tiles are NIGHT SHOWS posted in the evening, so the light and dark rhythm is also the posting rhythm. A ticket stub under each box numbers the show (SHOW 01 to 12, 'प्रयोग', the Marathi theatre word for a performance), and the season ends top-left on THE FINALE: the one show with a cast of three (the Ruby set, the BUY3 basket), bookending the opening curtain of Show 01 on the long diagonal.
why_better_than_A_and_B:
Read against the three judges (brand 81/78/69/64, reference craft 87/84/80/72, commerce 80/75/69/68) and the two front-runners they name, NAIRA MATCHING CENTRE (A, every lens's top or second) and MANGAL or THE NAIRA REISSUE (B):
1. MOTION IS THE IDEA, NOT A FORMAT. A had 2 reels and the craft judge called its P10 'the least conceptual reel across all four proposals'; B's best motion ideas (Reissue's matchbox drawer, MANGAL's antarpat drop) were single posts. Here all 12 posts move under one grammar (bells, pull, rise, bow, close), 7 reels and 5 carousels with 17 video slides, every reel loops seamlessly (its last frame is its first), and the tempo is the owner's own: drawer out 1.1 s and home 1.0 s, glint every 4 s, the 3.2 s float, clip-never-fade, all lifted from src/lib/nairaBox/config.ts.
2. THE EMBLEM IS THE BRAND'S REAL OBJECT, FIXED IN PLACE. The judges' main fix for A was 'the tag wanders' (it moves and rotates tile to tile); for the Fitting Book 'a 108x35 px label cannot carry the one-book read'; for the Reissue 'no cover carries the NAIRA wordmark'. Here the emblem is the box itself, same position and scale on 11 covers, about 215 px wide in the grid, and it carries the real wordmark on its lid (the lid counts as the frame's one wordmark, the rule the judges applied to box-lid photos).
3. IT OWNS A LANE NOBODY HAS: packaging as the stage. Unboxing is this account's only breakout topic (3,410 and 1,467 likes vs a 9.5 median). Retro's 'IT WAS ALWAYS A MATCHBOX' was judged one of the best motion ideas in the competition; this option builds the whole season on that insight instead of spending it on one post.
4. LOWER EXECUTION RISK THAN EITHER. A's danger was 'the humble institution done cheaply' and three AI textiles; MANGAL's was density, about 13 typefaces, ten unverified scripts and a dozen bespoke object drawings ('not safely a one-day build'). Here ONE stage kit (the site's CSS box ported to plain HTML + a paper-flat helper + slot reveal + glint) is built once and re-dressed 12 times; sets are flat cut-paper shapes (the register agents render well: silhouettes, lattices, panels) lit with real paper texture; no anatomy, no faces, no hands; three brand faces plus ONE Devanagari word (प्रयोग) that repeats on every ticket, so one native check covers the season.
5. EVERY TILE SELLS, AND THE BASKETS ARE THE STORY. No product-free tile (A's P11 was flagged). 15 named pieces, all in stock at 12 or more per variant, 8 of them Edition Two; the bestsellers lead (Prism, Woven, Ruby, Heartbead, Brushed Huggies); unsold deep stock gets jobs (Ruby necklace 70/0, Kiss Knot 40/0, Fine Tennis 20/0, Mint Pear 20/0, Silk Mesh 40/0, Bold Nocturne Drops 19/1). Baskets are built into the narrative: P3 four boxes for four people, P9 mismatched huggies (the listing's own styling tip, two pairs = BUY2), P12 the season's one cast of three (the Ruby set = BUY3, a payoff the grid has been setting up since the karwa wore the bracelet in Show 02). Gift posts land with delivery time: gifts 1 Nov, Bhai Dooj 3 Nov, wedding gift 20 Nov.
6. THE WIT IS AS INDIAN AS B AND AS TRUE AS A. Even the karwa dressed up; he will never say the line; the star stays in the locker; one bulb is always out; outfits don't repeat; you were Tree 3; the front row sees it all; rehearsals three weeks; the card came in a box. Each line is a shared memory for a 35 to 54 buyer, none mocks anyone, and the Cormorant turns are written as stage directions in parentheses, which is both the house voice ('(texture does the talking here.)') and how scripts are set.
7. THE GRID IS A COMPOSITION AT PROFILE SCALE: one shelf line per row, three colour columns in a checkerboard of value that grows out of LAC / flower / BONE, matinee and night-show tiles that match their posting times, dense-mid-quiet weight left to right in every row, and an opening curtain (bottom-right) answered by a curtain call (top-left).
8. A SOUND SIGNATURE. Three soft bells open every reel (the Marathi theatre's third bell), so the series is recognisable with the screen off.
why_it_fits:
BRAND. It is built from what the house already owns and has already tuned: the blush drawer box and its lid print, the CSS box in src/components/giftbox/NairaBoxCSS.tsx (proportions BOX w 1.6, d 1.6, h 0.7; card #D9BAB3, card-deep #C9A69E, rim #E8D2CB), the owner's motion numbers, the deck tulips and sage sprigs as painted scenery (never stuck on), Velista caps with a lowercase Cormorant turn, Jost labels, numbered series (the couture side's N° habit), sharp corners, the bracketed material kicker, the camp palettes (lac, red room, lilac, sage, bottle green). The wordmark appears only where the real box carries it. Nothing claims craft origin for the jewellery: the paper is ours, the pieces are named and described from their listings.
DATA. (a) Packaging is the one topic that broke out: 3,410 and 1,467 likes vs median 9.5. (b) The buyer is a woman 35 to 54 (64% of purchases), Maharashtra 46%: the season is staged in her calendar and memories (Marathi natak bells, Padwa and Bhaubeej, Aai and Vahini, the school annual day, the sangeet rehearsal, the box invitation). (c) What sells is one piece + one everyday Indian object + one witty line + one exact fact: each show has exactly that (the karwa, the script, the locker, the ladi, the school tree, the wedding chairs, the laser-cut card) and one listing fact on the end card. (d) Ruby is the hero stone and Edition Two is the season's story: Ruby opens the festive run (Show 02) and closes the season as a set (Show 12); 8 of the 15 pieces are Edition Two. (e) 69% of orders are one piece: 'cast of one' is the format, and the three basket shows are designed exceptions. (f) Sunday 12:00 and evenings 18:00 to 21:00 carry the orders: matinees post at 12:00, night shows at 17:00 to 19:00. (g) Reels sold reach, not baskets, in paid; so every reel ends on a programme card with the price and every guide is a carousel (stills plus loops), which is where 84% of purchases came from.
OWNER TASTE. Indian everyday wit with restraint; lilac (a whole lilac column); moody night grounds (lac, red room, plum, bottle green, deep sage); deck florals as scenery; clean, one piece per frame; exact facts; slow, calm motion at her own tempo; no lyrics; no black grounds, no sand or beige, no cool light, no faces, no stickers or stamps, no discount art.
REFERENCE. PTAT's system, Naira's own world: a recurring lockup on every tile (the box + ticket, where MILNI had the slab word + hand + marigolds), an event told in waves (twelve shows of one season), a drawn frame around a real thing (PTAT's drawn wardrobe around a real girl; here a paper set around a real piece), a steel-tray-style guide (the four-box tower), script + caps (Cormorant stage directions + Velista), named series and numbers (SHOW 01 to 12), big colour fields, reels in a designed grid.
motion_language:
THE HOUSE RITUAL (every reel; carousels use the same beats as loops). 0.00 HOUSE: the box shut, title above, footlights off; the shut box breathes (translateY 0 to -6 px and back over 3.2 s, its shadow scaling 1 to 0.96: the website box's HOVER period). 0.20 / 0.70 / 1.20 THREE BELLS (sound) with three light cues: bell 1 a warm wash rises behind the box (radial #FFF4E0, opacity 0 to .22); bell 2 the nine footlights on the drawer front's top lip come up (d 6 px dots, core #FFE8B0, 14 px glow, 0.3 s); bell 3 the title and stage direction exit upward through a mask (slide up 120 px, clipped, 0.6 s, cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1)). 1.50 to 2.60 THE PULL: the drawer slides out, 1.10 s, cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) (REVEAL.open, --nf-ease-reveal); the ribbon tab swings 6 degrees and settles. From 72% out (smoothstep 0.72, as on the site) THE RISE: paper flats hinge up from the stage plane back to front, rotateX 90 to -2 to 0 degrees about their base, 0.62 s each, ease-reveal, stagger 0.08 s: paper settles, it never bounces (overshoot 2 degrees max). THE ENTRANCE: the piece rises through a slot in the stage (translateY 100% to 0 inside an overflow-hidden window whose foot is the slot), 0.9 s, ease-reveal: the website ring's own rise. THE SCENE: one action per show (5 to 8 s). THE BOW: the piece dips 8 px and returns (0.5 s, ease-in-out) and the four-point glint (the site's GLINT: white core + two crossed lines, masked, scale 0.6 to 1 to 0.6, opacity 0 to 1 to 0 over 0.6 s) blooms on its brightest stone; while the piece is up the glint repeats every 4.0 s (REVEAL.glintEvery). THE CLOSE: the piece sinks through its slot (0.6 s), flats fold front to back (rotateX 0 to 90, 0.45 s, stagger 0.06 s), the drawer slides home in 1.0 s, ease-in-out (REVEAL.close), footlights dim. THE PROGRAMME (end card): name, price, one fact and nairaflore.com rise line by line through a slot in the title zone (0.6 s, stagger 0.08 s), the ticket rises from a slot under the shelf (0.5 s), hold 1.6 to 2.4 s. THE RETURN: programme exits up, title returns from below; the final frame is pixel-identical to the first, so Instagram's autoplay loop is seamless.
TEMPO CONSTANTS (owner-tuned, reused): drawer 1.1 s out / 1.0 s home; glint every 4 s; float 3.2 s; any continuous rotation at the box's 10.3 degrees/s (one turn per 35 s) and never faster than the header flower's 36 degrees/s (one turn per 10 s); stagger 30 to 80 ms; the only linear motion is constant motion (a moon rising, a scroll rolling, a light chasing).
EASING: entrances and the drawer cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); moves on screen cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1); constant motion linear; nothing ever eases in (no ease-in starts).
WHAT ENTERS HOW: pieces and text rise through slots; scenery hinges up (pop-up) or flies in on strings from above the frame (necklaces, ladis, the moon on its brass rod); props slide from the wings and are clipped by the drawer's side windows; light is the only thing allowed to fade (washes, glows, spot pools, stars, bulbs). This is the box's own rule: the ring is hidden by clipping planes, never by fading, because a fade left a ghost of it over the lid.
WHAT NEVER MOVES: the camera's seat (a fixed view from the stalls: rotateX -32 degrees, rotateY 0, perspective 6400 px, about 10.7x the lid width; a single push-in of at most 3% during the scene, returned before the close); the box's place on the shelf line; the lid print (never animated, never covered: every flat obeys the print-safe height rule); the ticket's position; type never animates letter by letter (except P4's script, typed by a left-to-right slot wipe because typing is its joke) and is never warped, bounced or scaled.
LOOP LOGIC: reels 14 to 18 s, last frame = first frame; carousel video slides 4 to 6 s at 1080x1440, first frame = last frame (slide 1's first frame is the designed cover, so the grid tile is exact); 30 fps; H.264 High, yuv420p, +faststart (tools/reel.cjs; add width and height arguments for 1080x1440, a one-line change).
SOUND: three soft brass hand-bell rings at 0.20, 0.70, 1.20 s open every reel (the series' signature); the drawer is a card-on-card slide; flats are soft paper flaps; the bow is one small glass 'ting'. Music from Instagram's library at posting, instrumental only, never lyrics: one instrument family per show (music box, santoor, sitar, harmonium, piano, tabla and claps, shehnai).

grid_system.type_system:
Three brand roles + one Devanagari word, nothing else (no Kalam, Rozha, Yatra, Playfair, DM Serif).
(1) VELISTA 400 (kit/fonts/Velista.woff2), CAPS ONLY, titles and the series name. Glyphs A-Z 0-9 . , ; : ! ? & ' " - ( ) @ # % / only: NO ₹, NO ·, NO °, NO accented letters (RIVIÈRE, PAVÉ and N° are always Jost). Cover titles 104 px (one-line titles 120 px), line-height 1.0, letter-spacing .02em, centred; reel titles 76 to 84 px. Every title ends with a full stop.
(2) CORMORANT GARAMOND ITALIC 400, lowercase, ALWAYS A STAGE DIRECTION IN PARENTHESES: '(the drawer is the stage.)'. 44 px on covers, 36 to 40 px in reels, 26 px on rod cards. This is the house's existing aside voice and how play scripts set directions, so the script + caps pairing has a reason.
(3) JOST (kit VF): labels 500 caps tracking .22 to .32em (13 to 30 px); support 400 (22 to 28 px); prices Jost 400 with font-family 'Jost','Poppins' so ₹ falls back to Poppins; piece names always in Jost caps, never Velista. Per frame: at most one eyebrow + two Jost lines (the end card is the programme, its own format).
(4) TIRO DEVANAGARI MARATHI 400, one word only, repeated on every ticket: प्रयोग (the Marathi theatre word for one performance of a play, as in 'the 500th प्रयोग'). One native check covers the season; P7's caption carries one Marathi greeting (दिवाळी पाडव्याच्या हार्दिक शुभेच्छा) that needs the same check. Nothing else in Indic script.
WORDMARK: only ever as the lid print on the box (kit/naira-wordmark.svg, #4A4440 at .86), so it appears once per frame by construction; never typed, never a second mark in the frame (P3's tower stacks the boxes so only the top lid shows; P12's season slide lists the shows in type rather than showing twelve lids). Punctuation: no em dashes, no exclamation marks, no emoji; middots only in Jost metadata.
grid_system.emblem:
THE BOX ITSELF, the real Naira packaging, in one fixed pose and place: a CSS 3D box ported from NairaBoxCSS.tsx (W = lid width, D = W, H = 0.4375 W), seen near-orthographically (perspective 6400 px, about 10.7 W, so the drawer does not balloon toward the lens; the site's 5 W was tested and reads like a corridor at this size), camera rotateX(-32deg) rotateY(0deg) so the drawer end faces the viewer squarely (symmetry; NAIRA on the lid reads upright from the drawer side, as on the real box). The lid print is kit/naira-wordmark.svg, #4A4440 at .86, 62% of the lid width, centred on the lid. PROTOTYPED (work/v3box/proto/p2-cover-proto.html): at W 640 the lid projects 350 px deep, the drawer front 246 px tall, and 380 px of drawer travel shows 240 px of stage; so the build uses W 600. GRID / COVER (1080x1440 tile): W 600, sleeve front-bottom edge centred at (540, 1046) (the SHELF LINE); shut, the box spans about y 494 to 1046; open (drawer travel E = 340) the stage spans about y 823 to 1035 and the drawer front reaches about y 1264, leaving the ticket at y 1308 to 1390 clear (measured in the prototype). REEL VIDEO (1080x1920 frames): the same W 600, sleeve front-bottom at (540, 1042), lid back edge about y 490, drawer front about y 1239 open (E = 320), all clear of Instagram's bottom UI. The box is the same size in the same place on 11 of 12 covers (P3 is the deliberate exception: four boxes stacked, W 300). At 391x521 the box is about 215 px wide and NAIRA on its lid about 135 px: tested legible at that size, and it is the real wordmark on the real object.
THE STAGE FLOOR: the real drawer bed is black velvet; on stage it is always covered by a PAPER FLOOR (a flat lying on the stage plane, inset 18 px from the drawer walls) in each show's floor colour, so the owner's 'no black grounds' holds and the floor becomes part of the set (P2 a terrace of tiles, P10 a rehearsal floor of tape, P1 ivory boards). Only the drawer's 18 px rim and a 4 px shadow at the sleeve edge show around it.
PRINT-SAFE RULE (keeps the wordmark visible behind every set, checked in the prototype): the print's front edge sits about 0.43 D (258 px) behind the lid's front edge, so a flat standing d px in front of the lid's front edge may be at most h = (258 + d) / 1.6 px tall (1/tan 32deg = 1.6): 161 px at the lid edge, 222 at d 100, 286 at d 200, 374 at d 340. Flats outside the print's x range (the lid's outer 19% each side) may be taller. Anything taller goes behind the box (rising above the lid into the sky: the moon) or flies in at the sides.

The ticket is ivory on every ground, so on night shows it is the one pale shape under the glowing box. At 36% it reads as a ticket shape with a number; the box above it carries the brand.
grid_system.recurring_devices:
Build these once as STAGE KIT (work/v3box/stage-kit/: box.js, flat.js, ritual.js, glint.js, ticket.js), then dress each show.
1 BOX: the port of NairaBoxCSS.tsx + pose.ts (faces as divs; the open drawer is the same convex box made longer and drawn through fixed windows, which keeps Chrome's face sorting clean), with four additions: the stage plane (the pulled-out top face) is where flats stand and is covered by the show's PAPER FLOOR (a flat lying on the plane, inset 18 px, AP-01 texture, the colour and pattern given per show); nine FOOTLIGHTS on the drawer front's top lip; and the RIBBON TAB on the drawer front (0.16 W x 0.055 W loop of #E9C2BA satin, from the 3D box's tab).
2 FLAT: a paper set piece (inline SVG path + fill + AP-01 texture at multiply .35 + 1.5 px edge highlight + drop-shadow 0 6px 10px rgba(30,15,10,.28) cast on the stage), parented to the stage plane at depth d with transform-origin at its base, animated rotateX 90 > -2 > 0. Heights obey the print-safe rule.
3 TRAP (slot reveal): an overflow-hidden window whose bottom edge is a line on the stage; the piece or text inside travels translateY 100% > 0. Pieces are 2D cut-outs turned to face the camera (the ring sprite's method, ringFacing = pose).
4 ROD CARD: a 220 x 110 ivory card (AP-01) on a 2 px brass #B0843A rod that rises from behind the box at stage left (x 90 to 310) or right (x 770 to 990): Jost 500 20 px caps label + Velista 36 to 44 px line + Cormorant 26 px direction. The toy theatre's placard. Max one per show (P7 uses two, one per encore).
5 FLY: thin threads (1.5 px #E9D9C6 at 70%) from above the frame that lower scenery or a necklace onto the stage (descend 0.9 s ease-reveal, settle sway 1.5 degrees).

posts.concept: The relaunch after 76 silent days, staged as the first night of a season. Every Naira piece already arrives in this blush box; today the box is a theatre and the audience is asked, politely, to sit down. The reel performs the whole house ritual once, slowly, so every later show can be shorter: three bells, the drawer slides out, a lac-red paper curtain rises on a backdrop painted with the brand deck's own coral tulips and sage blades, and the lead actor rises through the trap: the Prism Rivière Bracelet, whose three stone colours (aqua, soft pink, pale yellow) come back to it as three coloured stage lights that meet on it and mix to warm white. The joke is gentle and the idea is legible in three seconds: a jewellery box that is a stage, with a cast of one. The cover is the quietest tile of the season: the box shut, a line of warm light leaking at the drawer, the show about to start.

We went quiet for a while. Please take your seats.

Every Naira piece arrives in this blush box, with a drawer and a little ribbon to pull. This season we are opening it like a stage: twelve shows, three a week, one piece in each.

Tonight's cast of one is the Prism Rivière Bracelet: aqua, soft pink and pale yellow cushion-cut stones in one straight line, each in its own fine pavé halo, adjustable from 15 to 19 cm.

₹2,399. Free insured shipping and cash on delivery across India.

posts.why: It opens the grid after 76 days of silence (last post 9 Aug) while Meta keeps sending about ₹2.07 lakh of traffic to the profile, so P1 must explain the world and sell the piece people clicked. Prism Rivière is the #1 piece by revenue (14 units, ₹27,649 in 120 days), 67 in stock, a 9/10 market score; its story copy sold (11 purchases on ₹20k) where the price-led 'from ₹899' copy of the same image got 0 purchases, so the caption tells its facts, not its discount. The reel performs the full ritual once so viewers learn the grammar the next eleven posts rely on, and the bells become the series' sound. Packaging is the account's only breakout topic (unboxing reels 3,410 and 1,467 likes vs median 9.5). Tuesday 12:00 is a matinee slot inside the 12:00 to 21:00 window that carries 78% of orders. posts.concept: Karwa Chauth is the one night everyone dresses for the moon: the red saree, the mehendi, the bangles, the full shringaar. So on our stage, even the karwa (the spouted clay pot the fast is named for) is dressed: the Ruby Baguette Tennis Bracelet sits round its neck like the thread a karwa is usually tied with. The stage is a paper-cut terrace: a far skyline with lit windows, a parapet, a water tank, a TV antenna, a clothesline, and above it the star of the night, a paper moon on a brass rod that rises from behind the box, stops halfway (late, as every year) and only then comes up. Ruby is the hero stone and red is the night's colour; the joke is loving, not about anyone, and the piece is the punchline: the pot got the best seat and the best jewellery.

In the middle, on a plain paper necklace bust, the Bold Nocturne Chain never moves: 'a chain with enough presence to be the whole outfit', in its listing's words. The audience calls for an encore twice; the chain comes back both times. It also sets up the wedding season, where every function runs three days.

posts.caption:
Outfits don't repeat. Jewellery can.

In Maharashtra, Diwali takes two encores: Padwa today, Bhaubeej tomorrow. Three days, three outfits, one chain. The Bold Nocturne Chain is bold elongated paperclip links in warm gold tone, with one link set in clear cubic zirconia pavé, so a single point of sparkle breaks the run. posts.why: Posted at 12:00 on Padwa, between Diwali (8 Nov) and Bhaubeej (11 Nov): the 46% of buyers in Maharashtra (Mumbai and Nashik) live this three-day stretch, and the caption explains it for everyone else. 'Outfits don't repeat' is a near-universal social rule for Indian women at functions; turning it into a reason to own one strong piece is the house's 'worn, not saved' message with a joke. The Bold Nocturne Chain has 53 in stock and only 2 sold, and the trio has already sold as a BUY3 set: Show 10's drops complete it, and the caption cross-references. The scroll is the bioscope (the mela peep box) made literal, and the post pivots the feed from festival to the wedding season's three-day functions. Quiet tile in the right column.

posts.concept: Children's Day, for the person who actually buys: the mother who was once in the school annual day, playing Tree 3. Our stage is that school stage: dusty-rose paper curtains, a crayon forest on kraft paper, a crepe-paper sun on a stick, and three cardboard trees labelled TREE 1, TREE 2, TREE 3. Tree 3 has stage fright and trembles; its two leaves are the Mint Pear Drop Earrings (three small clear pears falling to one pale mint pear, like a leaf). Then Trees 1 and 2 slide into the wings, Tree 3 slides to centre stage, the spotlight lands, the audience claps and the tree bows. This year, you get the lead.

posts.alt_text: A blush pink Naira gift box on a deep lac red background, its drawer out like a stage under a gold-paper scalloped valance and a raised blush paper curtain, with a backdrop of painted coral tulips. posts.why: The top-left tile is what every visitor from an ad sees first from 22 Nov through the December muhurats, so it must sell the season's best basket: the Ruby set (₹5,198 list), built on the hero stone (Ruby 8 of 13 bracelets since 16 Oct; ruby huggies sold 3 of 3), the 70-unit necklace that has not sold once, and BUY3, the code the break-even maths needs (69% of orders are one piece). Bracelet + huggies is a known bought-together pair. The series' rule (cast of one) makes three pieces feel like an event, and the callbacks (Show 02's bracelet, Show 01's curtain and tulips) give the grid a memory. Sunday 19:00 is in the evening order peak on the strongest day. The lac ground rhymes with the LAC tile at the bottom of the same column.
posts.claims_check: Prices ₹2,300 / ₹1,699 / ₹1,199 (roster; every colour the same price); list total ₹5,198 shown (honest arithmetic, no discount, no strike); the BUY3 saving is never computed on the art. Ruby necklace 20, Ruby bracelet 12, Ruby huggies 12 on 25 Oct; stock guard above. 'Ruby-red baguette cubic zirconia', never 'ruby' as a stone; 'about 17 cm' (bracelet listing) and 'about 18 mm' (huggies listing); the necklace's length is not stated (its listing text is not in the snapshot; the alt text's 36 cm is not quoted). Tags 18k Gold Tone Plated, Edition Two on all three; no water or tarnish claim. The offer line is the exact approved line, caption only. Worn crops show no lips or eyes. The season slide lists titles in type; no second wordmark.

risks: BUILD: CSS 3D face sorting. Flats standing on the drawer plane share one preserve-3d context with the box; Chrome can mis-sort intersecting planes. Port NairaBoxCSS.tsx's convex-box approach exactly (the open drawer is the same box made longer, seen through fixed windows), keep every flat parallel to the drawer front, and check every 10th frame. Fallback if sorting fails: render the box's states once as PNG layers (shut, and drawer at each travel) and composite the flats in 2D with a scaleY hinge from their base; the camera never moves, so the fallback looks identical.

RENDER: tools/reel.cjs is fixed at 1080x1920; carousel loops need width and height arguments (1080x1440), a one-line change. About 3,400 reel frames plus 17 carousel loops at 30 fps; budget roughly 10 to 15 minutes of render per reel. End cards carry live prices baked into video: generate them from roster.json at render time and re-render any post whose price moved before it goes up.

INSTAGRAM: a carousel whose first slide is a video uses that video's first frame as the grid thumbnail; every slide 1 here starts on the designed cover, but test one draft before the rollout and fall back to a still slide 1 if the grid crops or picks another frame. Reel covers may not be editable after posting: upload the designed cover at publish time. Posting natively keeps 3:4; a scheduler may force 4:5, and everything critical sits inside y 45 to 1395.

CULTURE AND LANGUAGE: the 'third bell' convention of Marathi theatre (first comment of P1), the word प्रयोग on every ticket, and the Marathi Padwa greeting in P7's caption each need a native reader's sign-off before posting; if any fails, drop it (the ticket works without the word). The karwa wearing a bracelet (P2) is affectionate and decorative, but it touches a ritual object: owner to confirm. Tulsi Vivah is left alone (no product near the plant).

TONE: 'the understudy' (P5) could be read as calling the piece second-best. It is written as love for real gold plus the owner's own 'Not locker gold. Tuesday gold.'; if the owner prefers, the direction becomes '(the everyday one goes on every day.)' with the same visuals.

STOCK: Ruby variants (bracelet 12, huggies 12 on 25 Oct, selling about one a day) carry P2, P9's cover and P12. Each post has a written stock guard (swap to the Ruby necklace, to Emerald/Amethyst, or to the Crystal set) to be checked the evening before posting; no hero below 5. Every other piece has 19 or more in stock.

PACKING TRUTH: P3, P11 and P12 say 'every piece arrives in its own box'. Every listing promises 'You will receive your piece in a Naira Petite box', but the owner must confirm that multi-piece orders are packed one box per piece; if not, those lines become 'Every order arrives in the blush Naira box' (the visuals still hold).

THE VELVET: the real drawer bed is black velvet. The prototype showed a large black stage when it was left bare, so every show now lays a paper floor over it (terrace tiles, boards, a durrie, a runner); only the drawer's rim shows. The end cards and the caption never claim the floor is part of the packaging.

AI PLATES: 16 non-jewellery plates (20 credits); the gouache backdrops (AP-07 to AP-09), the crayon forest (AP-10) and the laser-cut props (AP-13, AP-14) are the most likely to read AI-made. Each has a flat SVG fallback (silhouette + paper texture). Nothing generated is jewellery, a face, a hand or text. P5's worn slide uses an existing Higgsfield plate (0711): check the braid against the listing before use, or swap to the real on-ear photo in a framed window.

SAMENESS: eleven covers share one box in one place. That is the emblem and the grid idea (a shelf of twelve theatres), but at a glance some may read it as repetitive; the variety is carried by twelve grounds in three colour columns, twelve box states and twelve set silhouettes, and P3 deliberately breaks the pattern. If the owner wants more contrast, two covers (P7, P10) can go to a close 'stage view' crop of the drawer without the full box, keeping the ticket.

PACE: the owner has sent back fast or jittery motion twice. Every timing here is slow (1.1 s drawer, 0.6 s hinges, 4 s glint cadence, at most 3% push-in); review every reel at full size and in slow motion before posting, and cut any scene that feels busy rather than speed it up.

SOUND: use Instagram's library tracks via the business account only (no lyrics; Indian labels have pursued brands over Reels music); bake only royalty-free effects (bells, drawer, paper, applause, glass ting) into the files, mixed under the music.

FONTS AND MARKS: Velista's licence for social use is unconfirmed (it is already used in every ad); Tiro Devanagari Marathi is a feed option pending the owner's sign-off. The wordmark appears only as the lid print; P3 hides lower lids and P12's season slide uses type, so no frame ever shows two marks.

CADENCE: post strictly P1 to P12, three a week, so each week completes one row; no pins during the rollout; if a post slips, use grid reordering rather than doubling up on a day. Captions name no delivery date; the festival gift posts leave the 3 to 5 working days delivery needs (P3 for Diwali, P4 for Bhai Dooj), and the wedding-gift posts aim at the late-November and December muhurats.

EFFORT: one stage kit (box, flats, slot, rod card, fly, light, glint, ticket, programme) built once, then twelve sets of three to six flats each; most set pieces are silhouettes, lattices and panels. A realistic agent build is two days for the kit and the first three shows, then about half a day per show, plus a native-language check and one owner review round.
